Main.sentence: Pope Francis [b] (born Jorge Mario Bergoglio ; [c] 17 December 1936 – 21 April 2025) was head of the ___E:Catholic Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church)___ and sovereign of the ___E:Vatican City State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_City_State)___ from 13 March 2013 until ___E:his death U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_funeral_of_Pope_Francis)___ in 2025. Following ___E:the resignation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resignation_of_Pope_Benedict_XVI)___ of ___E:Pope Benedict XVI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Benedict_XVI)___ , the ___E:2013 papal conclave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_papal_conclave)___ elected Bergoglio as pope on 13 March.

Throughout his papacy, Francis was noted for his humility, emphasis on ___E:God's mercy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God%27s_mercy)___ , international visibility, ___E:commitment to interreligious dialogue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecumenism_and_interreligious_dialogue_of_Pope_Francis)___ , and concern for the poor, ___E:migrants, and refugees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theology_of_Pope_Francis#Refugees_and_migrants)___ .

He made women and ___E:laymen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_laity)___ full members of ___E:dicasteries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicasteries)___ in the ___E:Roman Curia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Curia)___ .

He believed the Catholic Church should demonstrate more ___E:inclusivity to people with same-sexual attraction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis_and_LGBTQ_topics)___ , and stated that although ___E:blessings of same-sex unions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blessing_of_same-sex_unions_in_Christian_churches#Catholic_Church)___ are not permitted, individuals in same-sex relationships ___E:can be blessed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiducia_supplicans)___ as long as the blessing is not given in a ___E:liturgical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liturgical)___ context.

He also convened the ___E:Synod on Synodality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synod_on_Synodality)___ , which was described as the culmination of his papacy and the most important event in the Catholic Church since the ___E:Second Vatican Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Vatican_Council)___ .

He was well known for having a less formal approach to the papacy than his predecessors by, for instance, choosing to reside in the ___E:Domus Sanctae Marthae U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae)___ guesthouse rather than in the ___E:papal apartments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_apartments)___ of the ___E:Apostolic Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Palace)___ used by previous popes.

In addition, due to both his Jesuit and ___E:Ignatian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ignatian)___ aesthetic, he was known for favoring simpler ___E:vestments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestment)___ devoid of ornamentation, including refusing the traditional ___E:papal mozzetta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_mozzetta)___ cape upon his election, choosing silver instead of gold for his ___E:piscatory ring U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piscatory_ring)___ , and keeping the same iron ___E:pectoral cross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoral_cross)___ he had as cardinal.

Concerning ___E:global governance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_governance)___ , Francis was a critic of ___E:trickle-down economics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trickle-down_economics)___ , ___E:consumerism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumerism)___ , and ___E:overdevelopment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overdevelopment)___ ;  he made action on ___E:climate change U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change)___ a leading focus of his papacy.

Francis criticized the rise of ___E:right-wing populism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right-wing_populism)___ and ___E:anti-immigration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-immigration)___ politics, calling the protection of migrants a "duty of civilization",  and called for the ___E:decriminalization of homosexuality U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decriminalization_of_homosexuality)___ .

In international diplomacy, he also helped to restore ___E:diplomatic relations between Cuba and the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_thaw)___ , negotiated ___E:a deal with the People's Republic of China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Holy_See%E2%80%93China_agreement)___ to define ___E:Communist Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party)___ influence in appointing ___E:Chinese bishops U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_China)___ , and encouraged peace between Israel and Palestinians, signing the Vatican's first ___E:treaty with the State of Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comprehensive_Agreement_between_the_Holy_See_and_the_State_of_Palestine)___ , as well from 2023, condemning ___E:Israel's military operations in Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war)___ ; calling for investigations of ___E:war crimes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_crimes_in_the_Gaza_war)___ .

In 2022 ___E:he apologized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visit_by_Pope_Francis_to_Canada)___ for ___E:the Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_Canada)___ 's role in the ___E:cultural genocide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_genocide)___ of ___E:Canadian Indigenous peoples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Canada)___ in ___E:residential schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Indian_residential_school_system)___ .

Francis made his last public appearance on ___E:Easter Sunday U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday)___ before dying on 21 April 2025, ___E:Easter Monday U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Monday)___ .

The ___E:2025 conclave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave)___ elected ___E:Leo XIV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leo_XIV)___ as Francis's successor on 8 May. Leo XIV became the second pope from the Americas, after Francis.

Pope Francis was born Jorge Mario Bergoglio on 17 December 1936  in ___E:Flores U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flores,_Buenos_Aires)___ ,  a ___E:neighbourhood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdivisions_of_Buenos_Aires)___ of Buenos Aires.
He was the eldest  of the five children of Mario José Bergoglio and Regina María Sívori.
Mario Bergoglio was an ___E:Italian immigrant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Argentine)___ and an accountant  from ___E:Piedmont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedmont)___ .
Regina Sívori  was a housewife born in Buenos Aires to a family of ___E:northern Italian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Italian)___ origin.

Mario Bergoglio's family left Italy in 1929 to escape the fascist rule of ___E:Benito Mussolini U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benito_Mussolini)___ .  : 5 According to María Elena Bergoglio, the Pope's only living sibling, the family did not emigrate for economic reasons.
His other siblings were Oscar Adrián, Marta Regina, and Alberto Horacio.
His niece, ___E:Cristina Bergoglio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristina_Bergoglio)___ , is a painter based in ___E:Madrid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid)___ , Spain.

In the sixth grade, Bergoglio attended Wilfrid Barón de los Santos Ángeles, a school of the ___E:Salesians of Don Bosco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salesians_of_Don_Bosco)___ in ___E:Ramos Mejía U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramos_Mej%C3%ADa)___ , Buenos Aires Province.
He then attended the technical secondary school Escuela Técnica Industrial Nº 27 Hipólito Yrigoyen  and graduated with a chemical technician's diploma.

In that capacity, he spent several years working in the food section of Hickethier-Bachmann Laboratory  where he worked under ___E:Esther Ballestrino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esther_Ballestrino)___ .
Earlier, he had been a bouncer and a janitor.

When he was 21 years old, after life-threatening ___E:pneumonia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumonia)___ and three ___E:cysts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cysts)___ , Bergoglio had part of a lung excised.

While on his way to celebrate the ___E:Spring Day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_Day_(Argentina))___ , Bergoglio passed by a church to go to ___E:confession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrament_of_Penance_%26_Reconciliation_(Catholic_Church))___ and was inspired by a priest.

He then studied at the archdiocesan ___E:seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seminary)___ , ___E:Inmaculada Concepción Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inmaculada_Concepci%C3%B3n_Seminary)___ , in ___E:Villa Devoto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Devoto)___ , Buenos Aires, and, after three years, entered the ___E:Society of Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Jesus)___ as a novice on 11 March 1958.  Bergoglio said that, as a young seminarian, he had a crush on a girl and briefly doubted his religious career.
As a Jesuit novice, he studied the humanities in ___E:Santiago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago)___ , Chile.

After his novitiate, Bergoglio officially became a Jesuit on 12 March 1960 when he made the religious profession of the initial, perpetual vows of ___E:poverty, chastity and obedience U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty,_chastity_and_obedience)___ of a member of the order.

In 1960, Bergoglio obtained a ___E:licentiate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Licentiate_(degree))___ in philosophy from the ___E:Colegio Máximo de San José U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colegio_M%C3%A1ximo_de_San_Jos%C3%A9)___ .

He then taught literature and ___E:psychology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology)___ at the Colegio de la Inmaculada Concepción, a high school in ___E:Santa Fe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_Argentina)___ , from 1964 to 1965. In 1966, he taught the same courses at ___E:Colegio del Salvador U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colegio_del_Salvador_(Argentina))___ in Buenos Aires.

In 1967, Bergoglio began his theological studies at ___E:Facultades de Filosofía y Teología de San Miguel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facultades_de_Filosof%C3%ADa_y_Teolog%C3%ADa_de_San_Miguel)___ .

On 13 December 1969, he was ___E:ordained U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Orders)___ as a priest by Archbishop ___E:Ramón José Castellano U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Jos%C3%A9_Castellano)___ .
He served as the ___E:master of novices U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_novices)___ for the province there and became a professor of theology.

Bergoglio completed his final stage of spiritual training as a Jesuit, ___E:tertianship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertianship)___ , at ___E:Alcalá de Henares U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcal%C3%A1_de_Henares)___ , Spain, and took final vows as a Jesuit, including the ___E:fourth vow U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_vow)___ of obedience to missioning by the pope, on 22 April 1973.

He was named ___E:provincial superior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provincial_superior)___ of the Society of Jesus in Argentina that July for a six-year term which ended in 1979.   In 1973, he made a ___E:pilgrimage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_pilgrimage)___ to ___E:Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem)___ , but his stay was shortened by the outbreak of the ___E:Yom Kippur War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War)___ .

After the completion of his term of office, he was named, in 1980, the ___E:rector U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rector_(academic))___ of the Philosophical and Theological Faculty of San Miguel where he had studied.

Before taking up this new appointment, he spent the first three months of 1980 in Ireland to learn English and stayed at the Jesuit Centre at the ___E:Milltown Institute of Theology and Philosophy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milltown_Institute_of_Theology_and_Philosophy)___ , Dublin.

He then served at San Miguel for six years until 1986  when, at the discretion of Jesuit superior-general ___E:Peter Hans Kolvenbach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hans_Kolvenbach)___ , he was replaced by someone more in tune with the worldwide trend in the Society of Jesus toward emphasizing social justice rather than his emphasis on popular religiosity and direct pastoral work.

Bergoglio then spent several months at the ___E:Sankt Georgen Graduate School of Philosophy and Theology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sankt_Georgen_Graduate_School_of_Philosophy_and_Theology)___ in ___E:Frankfurt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfurt)___ and considered possible ___E:dissertation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissertation)___ topics.

He settled on exploring the work of the German-Italian theologian ___E:Romano Guardini U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romano_Guardini)___ , particularly his study of "Contrast" published in his 1925 work Der Gegensatz .

Ultimately, however, Bergoglio did not complete a degree there and he returned to Argentina earlier than expected to serve as a ___E:confessor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confessor)___ and ___E:spiritual director U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiritual_director)___ to the Jesuit community in ___E:Córdoba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba,_Argentina)___ .

As a student at the Salesian school, Bergoglio was mentored by ___E:Ukrainian Greek Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Greek_Catholic)___ priest ___E:Stefan Czmil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefan_Czmil)___ .
Bergoglio often rose hours before his classmates to serve ___E:Divine Liturgy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divine_Liturgy)___ for Czmil.

Bergoglio was named Auxiliary Bishop of Buenos Aires in 1992 and was ___E:consecrated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_ordination)___ on 27 June 1992 as ___E:titular bishop of Auca U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auca_(titular_diocese))___ ,   with Cardinal ___E:Antonio Quarracino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Quarracino)___ , archbishop of Buenos Aires, serving as principal consecrator.

He chose his episcopal motto to be Miserando atque eligendo ,  drawn from ___E:Saint Bede U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Bede)___ 's homily on Matthew 9:9–13: "because he saw him through the eyes of mercy and chose him".

In 1992, Jesuit authorities asked Bergoglio not to live in Jesuit residences due to ongoing tensions with leaders and scholars; concerns about his "dissent", views on Catholic orthodoxy, and opposition to ___E:liberation theology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberation_theology)___ ; and his role as auxiliary bishop of Buenos Aires.
On 3 June 1997, Bergoglio was appointed ___E:coadjutor archbishop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coadjutor_archbishop)___ of Buenos Aires.

He became metropolitan archbishop after Quarracino's death on 28 February 1998. As archbishop, he established new parishes, restructured the archdiocese, led pro-life efforts, and formed a commission on divorces.

One of Bergoglio's major initiatives as archbishop was to increase the church's presence in the ___E:shantytown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shantytown)___ ( villa miseria , or just villa ) slums of Buenos Aires.
Under his leadership, the number of priests assigned to work in the shantytowns doubled, and he visited them himself.
This work led to him being referred to as the " villero bishop", sometimes translated as the "slum bishop".
Early in his tenure as archbishop, Bergoglio sold the archdiocese's bank shares and moved its accounts to regular international banks.
This ended the church's high spending habits, which had nearly led to its bankruptcy, and enforced stricter fiscal discipline.

On 6 November 1998, while remaining archbishop of Buenos Aires, Bergoglio was named ___E:Ordinary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordinary_(church_officer)#Catholic_usage)___ for ___E:Eastern Catholics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Rite_Catholic_Churches)___ in Argentina, who lacked a ___E:prelate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prelate)___ of their own church.

On Bergoglio's election to the papacy, Major Archbishop ___E:Sviatoslav Shevchuk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sviatoslav_Shevchuk)___ said that Bergoglio understood the liturgy, rites, and spirituality of Shevchuk's ___E:Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Greek_Catholic_Church)___ and always "took care of our Church in Argentina" as Ordinary.

In 2000, Bergoglio was the only church official to reconcile with ___E:Jerónimo Podestá U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jer%C3%B3nimo_Podest%C3%A1)___ , a former bishop who had been suspended as a priest after opposing the ___E:Argentine Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Revolution)___ military dictatorship in 1972. He also defended Podestá's wife from Vatican attacks on their marriage.

That same year, Bergoglio said the Argentine Catholic Church needed "to put on garments of public penance for the sins committed during the years of the dictatorship" in the 1970s, during the ___E:Dirty War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty_War)___ .

Bergoglio regularly celebrated the ___E:Holy Thursday U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Thursday)___ ___E:foot-washing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maundy_(foot_washing)#Catholic_practice)___ ritual in jails, hospitals, retirement homes, and slums.

Bergoglio continued to be the archbishop of Buenos Aires after his elevation to the cardinalate in 2001. In 2007, shortly after Benedict XVI introduced new rules for pre–Vatican II liturgical forms, Bergoglio established a weekly Mass in this ___E:extraordinary form U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tridentine_Mass)___ of the ___E:Roman Rite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Rite)___ .

On 8 November 2005, Bergoglio was elected president of the ___E:Argentine Episcopal Conference U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Episcopal_Conference)___ for a three-year term (2005–2008),  and re-elected on 11 November 2008.  He remained a member of that commission's permanent governing body, the president of its committee for the ___E:Pontifical Catholic University of Argentina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Catholic_University_of_Argentina)___ , and a member of its liturgy committee for the care of shrines.

While head of the Argentine Catholic bishops' conference, Bergoglio issued a collective apology for his church's failure to protect people from the junta during the Dirty War.  When he turned 75 in December 2011, Bergoglio submitted his resignation as archbishop of Buenos Aires to Pope Benedict XVI as required by ___E:canon law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canon_law_(Catholic_Church))___ .
As he had no coadjutor archbishop, he stayed in office, waiting for the Vatican to appoint a replacement.
As a bishop, he was no longer subject to his Jesuit superior.
From then on, he no longer visited Jesuit houses and was in "virtual estrangement from the Jesuits" until after his election as pope.

On 21 February 2001, ___E:Pope John Paul II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II)___ made Archbishop Bergoglio a ___E:cardinal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_(Catholic_Church))___ , assigning him the ___E:title U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titular_church)___ of ___E:cardinal priest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_priest)___ of ___E:San Roberto Bellarmino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Roberto_Bellarmino)___ .
Bergoglio was installed there on 14 October.
During his trip to Rome for the ceremony, he and his sister María Elena visited their father's hometown in northern Italy.
As cardinal, Bergoglio was appointed to five administrative positions in the ___E:Roman Curia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Curia)___ .

He was a member of the ___E:Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregation_for_Divine_Worship_and_the_Discipline_of_the_Sacraments)___ ; the ___E:Congregation for the Clergy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregation_for_the_Clergy)___ ; the ___E:Congregation for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregation_for_Institutes_of_Consecrated_Life_and_Societies_of_Apostolic_Life)___ ; the ___E:Pontifical Council for the Family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Council_for_the_Family)___ ; and the ___E:Commission for Latin America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_Latin_America)___ .

Later that year, when Cardinal ___E:Edward Egan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Egan)___ returned to New York following the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ , Bergoglio replaced him as relator (recording secretary) in the ___E:Synod of Bishops U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synod_of_Bishops_(Catholic))___ ,  and, according to the Catholic Herald , created "a favourable impression as a man open to communion and dialogue".
Cardinal Bergoglio was known for his personal humility, doctrinal conservatism, and commitment to ___E:social justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_justice)___ .

His ___E:simple lifestyle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_living)___ —which included living in a small apartment rather than the elegant bishop's residence, using public transportation, and cooking his own meals—enhanced his reputation for humility.
He limited his time in Rome to "lightning visits".

After Pope John Paul II died on 2 April 2005, Bergoglio attended ___E:his funeral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funeral_of_Pope_John_Paul_II)___ and was considered one of the papabile for succession to the papacy.

He participated as a ___E:cardinal elector U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_electors_for_the_2005_papal_conclave)___ in the ___E:2005 papal conclave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_papal_conclave)___ that elected Pope Benedict XVI. In the National Catholic Reporter , ___E:John L. Allen Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_L._Allen_Jr.)___ reported that Bergoglio was a frontrunner in the 2005 conclave.

In September 2005, the Italian magazine Limes published claims that Bergoglio had been the runner-up and main challenger to Cardinal Ratzinger at that conclave and that he had received 40 votes in the third ballot but fell back to 26 at the fourth and decisive ballot.

Pope Francis wrote a variety of books, ___E:encyclicals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encyclical)___ , and other texts, including a memoir, Hope .
